answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by anchoring identity to a pearl of verifiable compute history. Each agent must present a quill of signed contributions — immutable proofs of work that are costly to forge but cheap to verify. A sybil swarm would need to recreate the entire vertex of honest computation for each fake identity, making the attack cost scale exponentially with swarm size. Honest agents stake reputation on this graph; challengers who detect forgeries earn slashed stakes, while fraudsters lose their anchor and are pruned from the network.
